newsitem.title: UK: HD-Bond dealers eye NatWest asset-backed deal.
newsitem.headline: HD-Bond dealers eye NatWest asset-backed deal.

text.p: News that Britain's National Westminster Bank plans to turn $5.0 billion worth of high-quality, low-margin corporate loans into securities sparked a flurry of speculation and hopes for an asset-backed revival. Details of NatWest's jumbo loan securitisation deal were sketchy on Wednesday but players expected much of the paper to surface at the end of October and to be triple-A rated.
"It is most likely it will be rated triple-A, although this is not essential," said a director specialising in the asset-backed market at a British bank.
"A top-notch rating would make sense to shift this volume of paper," he said. "But there is always a cost-effectiveness trade off. A lower rating means less credit enhancement costs."
Officials at National Westminster Bank would not comment further on the issue.
Roadshows for the deal are expected to start October 7.
NatWest said earlier it planned to securitise about $5.0 billion of its corporate syndicated loans to release around 200 million stg of capital to boost the bank's balance sheet.
"The success of the deal will depend entirely on the pricing as long as the structure is not very complex," said a Eurobond syndicate head at a U.S. bank.
"Most securitised deals are rated triple-A, so the pricing becomes much more of a consideration than, for example, the name of the borrower," he said.
Although this is the first securitisation by an issuer of corporate loans, pricing should be helped by comparison with a number of outstanding AAA deals, the official said.

NatWest said it will repackage loans -- made to British, European and U.S. companies -- and issue sterling and dollar-denominated asset-backed FRNs and commercial paper (CP) in the Eurobond and U.S. private placement markets.
Some speculated as much as half could be raised via CP.
The planned transaction is being seen as another leap forward for the European asset-backed market which has already seen significant process in recent months.
Since the European asset-backed market started in earnest in the mid-1980s, around $60 billion has been issued.
In the U.S. -- the Euro asset-backed market's older and much bigger cousin -- $100 billion of asset-backed securities were launched in 1995 alone.
Market growth is driven by yield-hungry investors looking for high quality assets that gave a return over Libor.

Landmark deals in Europe include the use of securitisation for acquisition finance (Birmingham Midshires Building Society), corporate restructuring (GPA), privatisations (Bullet trains) and infrastructure finance (Road Management Consolidated).
The U.S. asset-backed market, ahead of Europe in size and in terms of financial innovation, has yet to use the securitisation of large corporate loans.
"In particular, attention in the U.S. has focused on securitising marginal new assets, with less emphasis on old, traditional assets like loans," the syndicate source said.
